sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: As we go through life, other people often hold the keys to our success and happiness.
sentences.zh: 在我们的人生旅程中，其他人往往掌握着我们成功和幸福的钥匙。

sentences.en: In school, how your teachers think of you makes a difference in how they evaluate you.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，老师对你的看法会影响他们对你的评价。

sentences.en: Do they see you as a serious scholar or a disinterested student?
sentences.zh: 他们是把你视为一个刻苦的学者，还是一个漫不经心的学生？

sentences.en: As you grow older, you might try to impress someone whom you see as a potential romantic partner.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，你可能会试着给某个你认为具有潜在恋爱可能的人留下好印象。

sentences.en: You want this person to like you, to date you.
sentences.zh: 你希望这个人喜欢你，跟你约会。

sentences.en: In the workplace, we jockey for status and opportunities.
sentences.zh: 在职场中，我们为了地位和机遇勾心斗角。

sentences.en: We might ask a boss for a raise or a promotion.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会要求老板加薪或晋升。

sentences.en: How you come across to her will influence whether she says yes to you or tells you to take a hike.
sentences.zh: 你给她的第一印象将决定她是答应你的请求，还是让你一边凉快去。

sentences.en: Countless books and Reddit threads tell you how to navigate these waters.
sentences.zh: 无数的书籍和红迪网帖子都在教你如何应对这些复杂的局面。

sentences.en: A YouTube influencer might tell you to play nice.
sentences.zh: 油管网红可能会告诉你态度要好一点。

sentences.en: A TikTok star might recommend playing hardball.
sentences.zh: TikTok明星可能会建议你态度强硬。

sentences.en: Much of the advice you get will be contradicted by other advice you get.
sentences.zh: 你得到的许多建议都会与你听到的其他建议相矛盾。

sentences.en: In recent years, social scientists have started to study how we can more effectively influence how others think of us.
sentences.zh: 近年来，社会科学家开始研究我们如何才能更有效地影响别人对我们的看法。

sentences.en: They've discovered both pitfalls and opportunities in the way we go about trying to influence the opinions of people.
sentences.zh: 他们发现在我们试图影响他人意见时，既存在陷阱，也存在机遇。

sentences.en: Unlike a lot of what you hear on YouTube and TikTok, these researchers are not just sharing their personal opinions.
sentences.zh: 与你在YouTube和TikTok上听到的很多内容不同，这些研究人员并不仅仅是在分享他们的个人观点。

sentences.en: Their conclusions are guided by experimental evidence.
sentences.zh: 他们的结论是以实验证据为指导的。

sentences.en: The science of how to win friends and influence people.
sentences.zh: 关于如何赢得朋友并影响他人的科学。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》为您播出。

sentences.en: Let's say you have a job interview.
sentences.zh: 假设你要去参加一场工作面试。

sentences.en: How do you carry yourself?
sentences.zh: 你平时是如何展现自己的？

sentences.en: You might wear a nice outfit, walk into the room with your shoulders back, and offer a firm handshake.
sentences.zh: 你可能会穿一身漂亮的衣服，昂首挺胸地走进房间，并有力地与对方握手。

sentences.en: Or imagine you run into a neighbor.
sentences.zh: 或者想象一下你偶遇了一位邻居。

sentences.en: You smile at them, make small talk, give a friendly wave.
sentences.zh: 你对他们微笑，闲聊几句，友好地挥手致意。

sentences.en: What about buying a car?
sentences.zh: 买车呢？

sentences.en: Chances are you speak confidently to salesmen, so they offer you a good deal.
sentences.zh: 你很有可能会自信地与销售人员对话，这样他们就会给你一个好价钱。

sentences.en: Each of these is a small way we interact with other people.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们与他人互动的微小方式。

sentences.en: At the University of North Carolina, organizational psychologist Allison Fregale studies these interactions and how they shape what others think of us.
sentences.zh: 在北卡罗来纳大学，组织心理学家艾莉森·弗雷加尔专门研究这些互动以及它们如何塑造别人对我们的看法。

sentences.en: Allison Fregale, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·弗雷加尔，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: So great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Allison, I want to take you back to one of your early efforts to win friends and influence people.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，我想带你回想一下你早期试图赢得朋友和影响他人的经历之一。

sentences.en: In your sophomore year of high school, you decided to run for a position on your student council.
sentences.zh: 在你读高二的时候，你决定竞选学生会的一个职位。

sentences.en: What was the position you wanted, and how did it turn out?
sentences.zh: 你想要的职位是什么，结果怎么样？

sentences.en: Not well.
sentences.zh: 不太好。

sentences.en: I loSt.
sentences.zh: 我落选了。

sentences.en: I had a position my freshman year, decided I was going to run again for sophomore year, felt pretty confident, and was really surprised and disappointed that I didn't win.
sentences.zh: 我高一的时候当过一个职位，决定高二时再次参选，当时感觉挺有信心的，结果没当选，这让我感到非常惊讶和失望。

sentences.en: So the fires of your political ambition continued to burn bright, and you decided to give it another shot the following year.
sentences.zh: 所以你内心的政治野心之火依然熊熊燃烧，第二年你决定再试一次。

sentences.en: Did you decide to do anything differently?
sentences.zh: 你决定做出什么不同的举动吗？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我做了。

sentences.en: I was running for a junior vice president position, and because I thought I had been a little bit complacent in my sophomore year, I put a lot of work into my speech.
sentences.zh: 我当时在竞选高三副主席的职位，因为我觉得自己高二时有点太自满，所以我在演讲上花了很多功夫。

sentences.en: I thought, this is, you know, it's high school.
sentences.zh: 我想，这毕竟，你知道的，这只是高中。

sentences.en: It's all won and lost in the quality of that speech, and it's got to promise great things, and it also, importantly, has to be funny.
sentences.zh: 成败全在于那篇演讲的质量，它必须承诺带来美好的事物，而且同样重要的是，它必须有趣。

sentences.en: So I worked, and my mom tried to help me write a good speech.
sentences.zh: 所以我努力准备，我妈妈也尽力帮我写了一篇好演讲。

sentences.en: What did she come up with, or what did you come up with together?
sentences.zh: 她想出了什么点子，或者你们两个一起想出了什么？

sentences.en: Well, when I told her I was running for vice president, she thought about, you know, the presidency and said,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我告诉她我要竞选副主席时，她想到了总统，然后说，

sentences.en: what does the vice president even do except wait around for the president to die?
sentences.zh: 副主席除了等总统死还能干什么？

sentences.en: And I said, maybe that can go in the speech.
sentences.zh: 我说，也许这句话可以写进演讲稿里。

sentences.en: So I put in there something that seemed a lot funnier in high school, but it did land well,
sentences.zh: 所以我把那句话加了进去，在高中时它听起来要有趣得多，而且效果也确实不错，

sentences.en: which was that I was well prepared to step in in the event of the untimely death of our president.
sentences.zh: 那就是：在我们的总统不幸身亡的情况下，我已经做好了充分的准备来接替这个职位。

sentences.en: As I said, we were too young at that point to really have thought about, you know, our death and mortality.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，当时我们还太年轻，根本不会去考虑死亡和终将一死这种事。

sentences.en: But people thought it was funny.
sentences.zh: 但大家都觉得这很搞笑。

sentences.en: So I thought, I had a great joke.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时觉得，我有个绝妙的笑话。

sentences.en: I'm well known.
sentences.zh: 我很有名。

sentences.en: I'm liked.
sentences.zh: 大家都喜欢我。

sentences.en: I'm going to win this.
sentences.zh: 我这次稳赢了。

sentences.en: I do remember a friend of mine who I recently reconnected with.
sentences.zh: 我确实还记得我的一位朋友，我们最近重新取得了联系。

sentences.en: She was running unopposed in the same election.
sentences.zh: 她在同一次选举中是唯一候选人，没有竞争对手。

sentences.en: So she knew that she was going to have a position, and she was part of counting the votes.
sentences.zh: 所以她知道自己肯定能当选，而且她还参与了计票工作。

sentences.en: And I very much remember her coming into the student lounge after the speeches with the saddest look on her face, telling me everything I needed to know that I did not win.
sentences.zh: 我深深地记得她演讲结束后脸上带着极其悲伤的表情走进学生休息室，这把所有我需要知道我落选的事实都告诉我了。

sentences.en: She told me I had lost by a few votes, to whom I no longer remember.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我我以微弱票数落败，至于输给了谁我记不清了。

sentences.en: But my attempt was a failure.
sentences.zh: 但我的尝试以失败告终。

sentences.en: So I understand you were quite upset when you didn't win this race, and your mother gave you some advice.
sentences.zh: 所以我听说你在这次竞选失利时非常难过，你母亲给了你一些建议。

sentences.en: What did she tell you, Alison?
sentences.zh: 她对你说了什么，艾莉森？

sentences.en: She told me what mothers everywhere say and what I now repeat to my own kids.
sentences.zh: 她对我说的话是天下所有母亲都会说的话，也是我现在经常对自己的孩子重复的话。

sentences.en: She said, don't worry about what other people think of you.
sentences.zh: 她说，别管别人怎么看你。

sentences.en: You know, it's the kind of thing where all moms say it, and no kids actually ever feel one bit better about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是那种所有妈妈都会说，但没有哪个孩子真能因此感觉好受一点的话。

sentences.en: But I think that messaging was given to me at many different times of disappointment in my life.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在我人生中遇到许多次失望时，都听到过这样的话。

sentences.en: And as a parent, I get it.
sentences.zh: 作为一个父母，我完全理解。

sentences.en: You feel so bad for your kid when they're suffering.
sentences.zh: 当你的孩子遭受痛苦时，你会感到无比心疼。

sentences.en: And all you can tell them is to try to detach from the expectations or the judgment of the world around you.
sentences.zh: 你所能对他们说的，就是试着摆脱周围世界的期望或评判。

sentences.en: So you were not successful at changing how your classmates thought of you.
sentences.zh: 所以你并没有成功改变同学们对你的看法。

sentences.en: But many years later, you found yourself navigating a different problem that was also related to how people think of you.
sentences.zh: 但许多年后，你发现自己面临着另一个问题，这也与别人如何看待你有关。

sentences.en: It had to do with how you tell others where you went to grad school.
sentences.zh: 这与你如何告诉别人你在哪读的研究生有关。

sentences.en: Can you explain, Alison?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗，艾莉森？

sentences.en: Well, I've played introduction dodgeball for years and years, that when you meet somebody and they ask for something about you, like, where'd you go to college?
sentences.zh: 嗯，多年来我一直在玩介绍躲避球游戏，每当你遇到某人，他们问起你的个人情况，比如，你大学在哪里读的？

sentences.en: Where'd you grow up?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里长大的？

sentences.en: And I developed this habit of not liking to disclose where I went to school.
sentences.zh: 于是我养成了一种习惯，不喜欢透露我在哪里上学。

sentences.en: So I went to Dartmouth College for undergrad.
sentences.zh: 我的本科是达特茅斯学院。

sentences.en: I went to Stanford to get my PhD.
sentences.zh: 我在斯坦福大学获得了博士学位。

sentences.en: And when people would say things like, where'd you go?
sentences.zh: 每当人们问诸如“你在哪上学”之类的问题时，

sentences.en: I would give these vague answers like, oh, in the Northeast, in New Hampshire, on the West CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 我就会给出一些模棱两可的答案，比如，哦，在东北部，在新罕布什尔州，在西海岸。

sentences.en: And then they would have to pull it out of me.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就不得不一点点逼问我。

sentences.en: I remember sitting at a blackjack table in Las Vegas with a stranger asking me where I went to school.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次坐在拉斯维加斯的二十一点赌桌旁，一个陌生人问我在哪里上学。

sentences.en: And I didn't even want to tell this guy that I was never going to see again where I went.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不想把这个以后再也见不到的人告诉我在哪里读过书。

sentences.en: And finally, you know, I said, I went to Stanford.
sentences.zh: 最后，你知道的，我说，我去了斯坦福。

sentences.en: And then I immediately, he said, oh, that's very impressive.
sentences.zh: 然后我立刻，他说，哦，那太厉害了。

sentences.en: And then I immediately just went into downplaying it.
sentences.zh: 接着我马上就开始轻描淡写地掩饰。

sentences.en: Well, not really.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实也没什么。

sentences.en: You know, I, you know, I just, I applied on a whim.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我，你知道的，我只是，我当时是一时兴起申请的。

sentences.en: I had some story about how that no one should pay attention to that.
sentences.zh: 我编造了一些故事，说那没什么大不了的，谁也不用在意。

sentences.en: And every time I would have to say where I went to school, I would almost choke on the words and avoid eye contact.
sentences.zh: 每当我不得不说我在哪里上学时，我几乎都要卡壳，并且避开目光接触。

sentences.en: So why do you think you have played dodgeball when it comes to this question?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得为什么在面对这个问题时，你一直在玩躲避球呢？

sentences.en: What do you think you're trying to hide from others?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你在试图向别人隐瞒什么？

sentences.en: I feel really grateful and really privileged that I got to go to those institutions.
sentences.zh: 我为自己能够去这些学校上学感到非常感恩和荣幸。

sentences.en: But I never have been able to utter those words without thinking that I sound obnoxious and like a snob.
sentences.zh: 但我从来无法在说出这些话的同时，不觉得自己听起来很讨厌、像个势利小人。

sentences.en: And that's never my intention in any interaction to make anyone feel bad.
sentences.zh: 而在任何互动中，我的初衷绝不是让任何人感到难堪。

sentences.en: And so I developed this habit of just going to great lengths to disclose it and then only making situations more awkward.
sentences.zh: 所以我养成了这样一种习惯，不惜大费周章去隐瞒它，结果却让情况变得更加尴尬。

sentences.en: When other people would press, it would then just come off as weird.
sentences.zh: 当其他人继续追问时，这就会显得很诡异。

sentences.en: Why did I have to ask nine questions to get a basic fact out of you?
sentences.zh: 为什么我非得问九个问题才能从你这套出一个基本事实？

sentences.en: And I do it.
sentences.zh: 而我确实这么做了。

sentences.en: I will disclose it.
sentences.zh: 我还是会透露的。

sentences.en: That still makes me really uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 但这依然让我感到非常不舒服。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm also wondering if it can communicate the wrong message and a message that you were not trying to communicate at all,
sentences.zh: 是的，我也在想这是否会传达出错误的信息，一个你根本不想传达的信息，

sentences.en: which is, you know, that you at some level thought that you went to a better school than the other person asking you this question.
sentences.zh: 那就是，你知道的，你在某种程度上认为自己去的学校比向你提问的另一个人要好。

sentences.en: And you thought they would feel bad as a result of not having gone to such a good school.
sentences.zh: 你觉得他们会因为没有去过这么好的学校而感到难过。

sentences.en: And so you're trying to hide the fact that you went to an elite school in order to make them feel better.
sentences.zh: 所以你试图隐瞒自己上过精英学校的事实，好让他们感觉好受一些。

sentences.en: And in some ways,
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，

sentences.en: could you be communicating to them in some ways that you actually have a hierarchy of schools in mind and that you actually thought that you did go to a better school?
sentences.zh: 你是否在某种程度上向他们传达了这样的信息：你的心中其实存在着学校的等级之分，并且你真的认为自己确实去了一所更好的学校？

sentences.en: I think it's that's very much true, because now as we're talking this and I think when someone then first discloses to me, oh, I went to Harvard or I went to Yale or something,
sentences.zh: 我想这确实很对，因为现在当我们这样谈论时，我想当有人第一次向我透露，哦，我去了哈佛或者我去了耶鲁之类的时候，

sentences.en: I am much more likely to feel comfortable disclosing in exchange.
sentences.zh: 我更有可能会感到舒适，从而也愿意礼尚往来地坦白。

sentences.en: So I do think there's probably an underlying assumption that if I'm talking to somebody I know nothing about,
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，可能存在这样一种潜在的假设：如果我在和一个一无所知的人说话，

sentences.en: chances are statistically they didn't go to a school that was as highly ranked.
sentences.zh: 从统计学上讲，他们大概率没有去过排名那么高的学校。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't want to be in a situation where I was saying that I had done something that was that was better.
sentences.zh: 而我不想陷入那种宣称自己做过更了不起的事情的境地。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But of course, once they find out that you did go to Dartmouth and to Stanford, then they not only know that you went to Dartmouth and to Stanford,
sentences.zh: 但当然，一旦他们发现你确实去过达特茅斯和斯坦福，他们不仅知道你去了达特茅斯和斯坦福，

sentences.en: but they know that you think that they might have thought that they might have looked inferior if you told them that you went to Dartmouth or Stanford.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还知道你觉得他们可能会这么想——如果你告诉他们你去了达特茅斯或斯坦福，他们可能会觉得自己低人一等。

sentences.en: It's not a winning strategy, but I just have come to see how many times I confronted and it makes me uncomfortable and I start playing dodgeball.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个制胜的策略，但我只是逐渐意识到我曾多次面对这种情况，这让我感到很不舒服，于是我开始玩起躲避球。

sentences.en: So these stories reveal the potential errors we make and how we seek to influence what others think of us.
sentences.zh: 所以这些故事揭示了我们在试图影响别人对我们的看法时可能犯下的错误。

sentences.en: I want to look at a couple of other examples before we get to the science of what is underlying these interactions.
sentences.zh: 在探讨这些互动背后的科学原理之前，我想先看几个其他的例子。

sentences.en: Early in your teaching career, Alison, you won a prestigious teaching award.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，在你教学生涯的早期，你获得了一项声誉卓著的教学奖。

sentences.en: What was this award and how did winning make you feel?
sentences.zh: 这是一个什么奖项，获奖让你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: My second year as a professor, I won what's called the Weatherspoon Teaching Award.
sentences.zh: 在我担任教授的第二年，我获得了所谓的威瑟斯poon教学奖。

sentences.en: There are several of them at the University of North Carolina named for the wonderful benefactor who funded them.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳大学有好几个这样的奖项，都是以资助它们的慷慨捐助者的名字命名的。

sentences.en: And I won the one for undergraduate teaching, which was the course I was teaching when I started at UNC.
sentences.zh: 我获得了本科教学奖，这也是我刚到北卡罗来纳大学时教的课程。

sentences.en: So I was in my second year and I won this prestigious award.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时正处于第二年，然后我赢得了这个声誉崇高的奖项。

sentences.en: So one person wins in every teaching category each year.
sentences.zh: 所以每年每个教学类别只有一个人获奖。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So this is a big deal because to win in your second year means that you really made a very strong impression in your first year.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件大事，因为能在第二年获奖意味着你在第一年确实留下了非常深刻的印象。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I felt good about it, especially because I came into UNC.
sentences.zh: 我对此感觉很好，尤其是因为我刚来到北卡罗来纳大学时，

sentences.en: See, I had never taught a single day in my life because my graduate program didn't give me that opportunity.
sentences.zh: 看吧，我以前从来没有教过哪怕一天的书，因为我的研究生项目没有给我提供过这样的机会。

sentences.en: So I went from never teaching in year one to winning an award in year two.
sentences.zh: 所以我从第一年从没教过书，到第二年就赢得了奖项。

sentences.en: And I did feel very proud about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此确实感到非常骄傲。

sentences.en: And I felt that I had actually earned it because I put a lot of my heart and effort into making that class really great.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我是实至名归的，因为我倾注了大量的心血和努力来把那门课上得极其精彩。

sentences.en: Alison continued to be a great teacher.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森继续做着一位出色的老师。

sentences.en: But as the months unfolded, something strange happened.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，几个月过去了，奇怪的事情发生了。

sentences.en: Year three, she didn't win another teaching award.
sentences.zh: 第三年，她没有再赢得教学奖。

sentences.en: Year four, same thing.
sentences.zh: 第四年，同样如此。

sentences.en: Year five?
sentences.zh: 第五年呢？

sentences.en: I'd come off of winning one award, so I thought winning awards wasn't really that hard to do.
sentences.zh: 我刚拿过一个奖，所以我以为获奖其实并不是那么难的一件事。

sentences.en: And I started to think about, surely I'm going to get recognized at some point.
sentences.zh: 我开始想，我总归在某个时刻会得到认可的。

sentences.en: They're going to run out of people to award.
sentences.zh: 他们总会把能发奖的人发完的。

sentences.en: The school's only so big, if nothing else, the process of elimination.
sentences.zh: 学校就这么大，别的不说，用排除法也该轮到我了。

sentences.en: So I was always happy because the other people who would win were also amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是很高兴，因为其他获奖的人也同样非常优秀。

sentences.en: So there was never any, I'm definitely a better teacher than that person because that's not true.
sentences.zh: 所以从来没有什么“我绝对比那个人教得好”的想法，因为那不是真的。

sentences.en: But there was a part of me that always thought, surely at some point I'm going to have to win because I do a really good job at this.
sentences.zh: 但我的内心深处总是在想，总有一天我肯定得获奖，因为我这方面的工作做得真的很好。

sentences.en: So a senior colleague comes up to you at one point and makes an interesting suggestion.
sentences.zh: 于是，一位资深同事在某个时候找到了你，并提出了一个有趣的建议。

sentences.en: Tell me what the suggestion was and how you responded.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我那是什么建议以及你是如何回应的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so my friend, who's the chair of my area at the time, comes into my office at the school, shuts the doors, something bad is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 好的，当时我所在领域的系主任走进我在学校的办公室，把门关上，这预示着有不好的事情要发生了。

sentences.en: But he says something very kind.
sentences.zh: 但他却说了一些非常温暖的话。

sentences.en: He said, I had been teaching this required course.
sentences.zh: 他说，我之前一直在教这门必修课。

sentences.en: I was getting ready to transition out of it, hand it over to someone else.
sentences.zh: 我正准备不再教这门课，把它交接给其他人。

sentences.en: And he said, you haven't won this award yet.
sentences.zh: 他说，你还没赢得过这个奖项呢。

sentences.en: And would you like me to put together a group of people to nominate you for the award,
sentences.zh: 你愿不愿意让我组建一个团队来提名你获得这个奖项，

sentences.en: essentially to court nominations so that the award committee would see not just one or two letters, but 10 or 12 letters just from students, from faculty, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 本质上就是去争取提名，这样评奖委员会看到的就不只是那一两封信，而是来自学生、教职员工等群体的10到12封推荐信。

sentences.en: And it was a very, very kind, nice offer coming from a place of respect, I think, for the work that I had done.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常、非常亲切、美好的提议，体现了对我和我所做工作的尊重。

sentences.en: And did you jump at this opportunity?
sentences.zh: 那你当时立刻抓住这个机会了吗？

sentences.en: I didn't.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: I had the opposite reaction.
sentences.zh: 我有截然相反的反应。

sentences.en: And I feel a little, I said, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有点……我说，绝对不行。

sentences.en: And my facial expression, like, you know, led on some kind of offense.
sentences.zh: 我的面部表情，你知道的，表现出某种被冒犯的样子。

sentences.en: Like, this was the most unethical, terrible idea I had ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 就好像这是我听过的最不道德、最糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: And I don't know if this person who was asking me had done it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道向我提出这个请求的人自己有没有这么做过。

sentences.en: But I came to find out that lots of people did this.
sentences.zh: 但后来我发现很多人都这么做。

sentences.en: And I think in my reaction, it was almost offensive.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的反应几乎是带有攻击性的。

sentences.en: Like, this thing that many people were doing, which was creating these nominating committees, was so off-putting to me.
sentences.zh: 就好像许多人在做的这件事——也就是组建这些提名委员会——让我感到非常反感。

sentences.en: So I said, no thanks.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，不用了谢谢。

sentences.en: I'm not interested.
sentences.zh: 我没兴趣。

sentences.en: I don't want to win it that way.
sentences.zh: 我不想用这种方式获奖。

sentences.en: So you wanted to win it in a way where you played no role whatsoever in engineering it.
sentences.zh: 所以你想以一种完全不参与策划的方式获奖。

sentences.en: You just wanted to happen organically.
sentences.zh: 你只想让它自然而然地发生。

sentences.en: I had this belief that that was how the people were winning,
sentences.zh: 我当时坚信其他人获奖的方式是，

sentences.en: was that students were just so moved by your teaching that they would just run forward at this nomination process en masse and write these glowing letters.
sentences.zh: 学生们被你的教学深深打动，以至于他们会自发地大量涌来参与提名流程，并写出这些热情洋溢的信件。

sentences.en: And the committee would read letter after letter of a grateful student, and they would have no choice but to award you this.
sentences.zh: 然后委员会就会一封接一封地阅读感激学生的来信，他们别无选择，只能将这个奖项颁给你。

sentences.en: But that really wasn't how these things were actually happening.
sentences.zh: 但这些事情实际发生的方式并非如此。

sentences.en: It was genuine, and it was people saying, this person really deserves to win, so let's put together a strategic approach for helping show this person's great work.
sentences.zh: 这是真诚的，是人们在说，这个人真的配得上获奖，所以让我们制定一个战略方案来帮助展现这个人的卓越工作。

sentences.en: But it felt icky to me.
sentences.zh: 但这让我觉得很别扭、很恶心。

sentences.en: Allison's experiences are hardly unique.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森的经历绝非个例。

sentences.en: When it comes to showcasing our achievements or telling other people about our accomplishments, we often do one of two things.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到展示我们的成就或向他人讲述我们的功绩时，我们通常会做以下两件事之一。

sentences.en: Sometimes, we come across as boastful.
sentences.zh: 有时，我们会显得自吹自擂。

sentences.en: Other times, we are so afraid about coming across as boastful that we hide our achievements under a rock.
sentences.zh: 而另一些时候，我们又极其害怕显得自吹自擂，以至于把自己的成就藏在石头底下。

sentences.en: We expect the world to discover our genius and come knocking on our door with accolades.
sentences.zh: 我们期待世界发现我们的天才，然后带着赞誉来敲响我们的门。

sentences.en: In time, after Allison became a researcher who studies how people win and lose respect, she realized not just that both strategies were flawed, but why they were flawed.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，艾莉森成为了一名研究人们如何赢得和失去尊重的研究人员，她不仅意识到这两种策略都有缺陷，还知道了它们为什么有缺陷。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: In one of Aesop's fables, a donkey finds the skin of a lion left in the forest by a hunter.
sentences.zh: 在伊索寓言中，一头驴子在森林里发现了一张猎人留下的狮子皮。

sentences.en: The donkey decides to try it on.
sentences.zh: 驴子决定试穿一下。

sentences.en: He hides in a thicket, and as various animals walk by, he jumps out and scares them out of their wits.
sentences.zh: 它躲在灌木丛中，当各种动物走过时，它突然跳出来，把它们吓得魂飞魄散。

sentences.en: The scam works perfectly until the donkey breaks out in laughter at his frightened victiMs.
sentences.zh: 这个恶作剧非常成功，直到驴子看着被吓坏的受害者，忍不住放声大笑。

sentences.en: His braids echo through the foreSt.
sentences.zh: 它的叫声在森林中回荡。

sentences.en: A fox walking by gives him some advice.
sentences.zh: 一只路过的狐狸给了它一些建议。

sentences.en: If you had kept your mouth shut, you might have frightened me too, but you gave yourself away with that silly braid.
sentences.zh: 如果你闭紧嘴巴，说不定也能把我吓跑，但你那愚蠢的叫声暴露了你自己。

sentences.en: How do you want others to see you?
sentences.zh: 你希望别人怎么看你？

sentences.en: As a powerful lion?
sentences.zh: 是一个强大的狮子？

sentences.en: A generous friend?
sentences.zh: 还是一个慷慨的朋友？

sentences.en: A confident colleague?
sentences.zh: 亦或是一个自信的同事？

sentences.en: Organizational psychologist Allison Fregale says like that donkey in the story, most of us undermine our own efforts to get people to see us the way we want to be seen.
sentences.zh: 组织心理学家艾莉森·弗雷加尔说，就像故事里的那头驴子一样，我们大多数人都破坏了自己让别人按我们希望的方式看待我们的努力。

sentences.en: Allison, I want to go back to the advice your mother gave you in high school when you lost that election for vice president.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，我想回到你在高中竞选副总统落选时你母亲给你的建议。

sentences.en: She told you not to worry about what other people thought of you.
sentences.zh: 她叫你不要在意别人怎么看你。

sentences.en: Was it good advice?
sentences.zh: 这是一个好建议吗？

sentences.en: It's kind, but if it's taken the way most people take it, it's not good advice because it tells us that we should ignore or stop trying to influence how other people see us.
sentences.zh: 它充满善意，但如果按照大多数人的理解去接受它，这就不是一个好建议，因为它告诉我们应该忽视或停止试图影响别人如何看待我们。

sentences.en: And I do think that is bad advice.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为这是一个糟糕的建议。

sentences.en: And do you think it's bad advice because that's an impossibility for us that we are a social species that other people's opinions of us do matter and asking us to ignore those opinions in some ways,
sentences.zh: 你认为这是个糟糕的建议，是因为对我们来说这是不可能做到的吗？我们是社会性动物，别人对我们的看法确实很重要，而要求我们某种程度上忽视这些看法，

sentences.en: you know, goes against every part of our social being?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这违背了我们社会属性的每一个部分？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because when we think about how many impressions we carry of other people, so if we use ourselves, those impressions guide our behavior.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们想到我们对其他人抱有成千上万种印象时，如果我们以自己为例，这些印象就会指导我们的行为。

sentences.en: And so when you are negotiating with somebody, if you don't trust that person, if you don't like that person,
sentences.zh: 因此，当你与某人谈判时，如果你不信任那个人，如果你不喜欢那个人，

sentences.en: the thoughts in your head about that other person have a great impact on whether or not you're going to be able to reach an agreement and whether or not it's going to be good.
sentences.zh: 你脑海中关于那个人的想法，会对你是否能达成协议以及协议是否会好产生巨大影响。

sentences.en: And so if we get into this logic, which I understand it's a lure, is that we don't have to care about what other people think or don't worry about what other people think,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们陷入这种逻辑——我理解它很有诱惑力——即我们不必关心别人怎么想，或者不用担心别人怎么想，

sentences.en: it can lead us to some really suboptimal problematic strategies that don't serve us well.
sentences.zh: 它可能会导致我们采取一些真正非最优的、有问题的策略，这些策略对我们没有好处。

sentences.en: And then we're left confused as to why it didn't get a good outcome.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会对为什么没有取得好结果感到困惑。

sentences.en: So you've become interested in studying something that many people would like to pretend doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始研究许多人愿意假装它并不重要的事情。

sentences.en: You study status.
sentences.zh: 你研究地位。

sentences.en: What do you mean by status, Alison?
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，你所说的地位是什么意思？

sentences.en: Status, the way we study it, is the respect and regard that others have for us.
sentences.zh: 我们所研究的地位，是别人对我们的尊重和敬重。

sentences.en: So my status is how much other people respect and regard me.
sentences.zh: 所以我的地位就是别人多么尊重和敬重我。

sentences.en: Your status is how much other people respect and regard you.
sentences.zh: 你的地位就是别人多么尊重和敬重你。

sentences.en: So when people say they don't care about status or that status doesn't matter, you sometimes cite the words of a 16th century English playwright.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们说他们不在乎地位或者地位不重要时，你有时会引用一位16世纪英国剧作家的话。

sentences.en: What did Christopher Marlowe have to say about status?
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗·马洛对地位有什么看法？

sentences.en: He allegedly said, and it turns out that it's very problematic to quote long dead people because there's very little Internet record of it.
sentences.zh: 他据称说过——事实证明，引用早已去世的人的话是非常有问题的，因为互联网上关于他的记录非常少。

sentences.en: But allegedly, he said, we control 50% of a relationship.
sentences.zh: 但据称他说过，我们控制一段关系中的50%。

sentences.en: We influence 100% of it.
sentences.zh: 我们影响着它的100%。

sentences.en: And I think that's really wise advice, which is when it comes to status, it exists only in other people's minds, but its effects are very real and significant.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常明智的建议，也就是说，谈到地位时，它只存在于别人的脑海中，但它的影响是非常真实且显著的。

sentences.en: And we can influence it.
sentences.zh: 而且我们可以影响它。

sentences.en: We cannot guarantee that another human being will give us respect and regard.
sentences.zh: 我们无法保证另一个人会给予我们尊重和敬重。

sentences.en: But we can do things that make it more likely that that will be the case.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以做一些事情，让这种可能性变得更高。

sentences.en: So let's look at some of the ways that can make it more or less likely that we can change how other people think of us.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们来看看一些能让我们更有可能或更不可能改变别人对我们的看法的方法。

sentences.en: One way we try to protect our status is by demonstrating that we are smart and competent people.
sentences.zh: 我们试图保护自己地位的一种方法是证明我们是聪明且能干的人。

sentences.en: But the way we do this often doesn't communicate what we think it communicates.
sentences.zh: 但我们这样做的方式往往无法传达我们自以为传达的信息。

sentences.en: I understand this once happened to you in a conversation you had with an employee of yours, your nanny.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，这曾经发生在你与你的一个员工——你的保姆的一次对话中。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I love to be correct or more accurately, I should say, I find it really hard to be told that I've done something incorrectly.
sentences.zh: 是的，我喜欢做对的事情，或者更准确地说，我应该说，我发现自己很难接受别人说我做错了事。

sentences.en: I've made a mistake because I feel like I do work so hard to try to get all the things done and do all the right things.
sentences.zh: 我犯了错误，因为我觉得为了把所有事情做好、做所有正确的事，我真的付出了很多努力。

sentences.en: And so I was on the phone with my nanny.
sentences.zh: 当时我正和保姆通电话。

sentences.en: I was on the speakerphone, my oldest child who's 15 is in the car, and I'm leaving on a 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我开着免提，我15岁的大儿子在车里，而我第二天早上6点就要坐飞机离开。

sentences.en: flight the next morning.
sentences.zh: 我说了类似这样的话：你明天早上6点45分要来这里带孩子去上学。

sentences.en: And I said something like, you're going to be here at 6.45 in the morning to take the kids to school.
sentences.zh: 她说，我想可能是这样，因为我在你的日程表上看到你要离开。

sentences.en: And she said, I figured that might be the case because I saw it on your calendar that you were leaving.
sentences.zh: 是的，我可以去。

sentences.en: Yes, I can be there.
sentences.zh: 我说，什么叫你想可能是这样？

sentences.en: And I said, what do you mean you figured it might be the case?
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过这事的，你说过你要来。

sentences.en: We talked about it and you said that you were going to come.
sentences.zh: 她说，我不记得了。

sentences.en: And she said, I don't remember that.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我的第一反应是——我对她这么说了，我说，

sentences.en: And to me, my first thought was, and I said this to her, I said,
sentences.zh: 对我来说非常重要的是，你知道我不是那种一声不吭离开镇、然后假设你会在半夜赶来的人。

sentences.en: it's really important to me that you know that I don't just leave town and assume that you're going to come in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 我不会在不告诉你地情况下对你做这种事的。

sentences.en: I would not have done that to you without telling you.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得我告诉你了。

sentences.en: I really feel like I told you.
sentences.zh: 她说，我不记得了，但她接着说，这没关系。

sentences.en: She said, I don't remember, but she said, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我有空做这件事。

sentences.en: Either way, I'm available to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以没有任何问题。

sentences.en: So there was no problem.
sentences.zh: 她会来的。

sentences.en: She was coming.
sentences.zh: 她看起来没有生气。

sentences.en: She didn't seem aggravated.
sentences.zh: 我们已经合作多年了。

sentences.en: We've worked together for years.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，“我不是对的”、“我做了这样一件事”的想法是如此令人不安，以至于我把车停在了路边。

sentences.en: But to me, the idea that I was not correct, that I had done something like this, was so disturbing that I pulled the car over on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 我儿子问，我们为什么要停车？

sentences.en: And my son said, why are we stopping?
sentences.zh: 我说，因为我知道我告诉过她。

sentences.en: I said, because I know I told her.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的第一件事就是在我的电子邮件中搜索。

sentences.en: So first thing I do is I search through my emails.
sentences.zh: 我没找到。

sentences.en: I don't find it.
sentences.zh: 然后我不得不翻看短信记录，这搜索起来极其不方便。

sentences.en: So then I have to go through the text thread, which is incredibly inconvenient to search.
sentences.zh: 但在那里我找到了。

sentences.en: But there I find it.
sentences.zh: 往上滑动几下拇指，就是我对她说：你能在某一天（星期四？）6点45分来吗？

sentences.en: A few thumb swipes up is me saying to her, can you come at 645 on whatever day it was, Thursday?
sentences.zh: 她说，好的，没问题。

sentences.en: And she said, yes, not a problem.
sentences.zh: 我会把它记在日程表上。

sentences.en: I'll put it in the calendar.
sentences.zh: 然后，仅仅知道我告诉过她还不够，我截了图，又发短信给她。

sentences.en: And then, and that wasn't enough just to know that I had told her, I screenshotted it, and I texted it back to her.
sentences.zh: 我说，你看，我确实跟你说过这个。

sentences.en: And I said, see, I did tell you this.
sentences.zh: 我情不自禁地这么做了，尽管正如我跟你讲述的那样，这在任何人看来都不是很好看。

sentences.en: And I couldn't help myself, even though, as I tell it to you, like, that doesn't look very good on anyone.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得，不，根本没必要这样做。

sentences.en: And you're like, no, there was no need for that.
sentences.zh: 但我还是做了。

sentences.en: But I did.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你既专注于显得能干，同时也专注于证明你不是一个冷酷无情的雇主。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you are focused both on looking competent, but also on demonstrating that you're not a cruel employer.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在证明，你之前一直在体谅她。

sentences.en: You are demonstrating that, in fact, that you had been considerate of her earlier.
sentences.zh: 这就是你当时想这么做的动机。

sentences.en: That was your motivation in wanting to do this.
sentences.zh: 但你认为她看到你发送的这条信息、这个截图时会有什么感想？那截图基本上是在说：看，我们有过这段短信交流。

sentences.en: But how do you think she saw this note that you sent her, this screenshot, which basically said, look, we had this text exchange.
sentences.zh: 而且你事实上已经同意在这一天来了。

sentences.en: And you, in fact, agreed to come on this day.
sentences.zh: 所以我不能百分之百确定。

sentences.en: So, I don't know for sure.
sentences.zh: 我没有问，我只是对整件事感到尴尬。

sentences.en: I didn't ask, I just felt embarrassed by the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我的本质做法就是在说：我是对的，你是错的。

sentences.en: But I think that essentially what I was doing was saying, I was right, you were wrong.
sentences.zh: 这就是这种沟通传达的概念。

sentences.en: That's the notion of the communication.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我处于那种情况时，我对这个人并没有多少好感。

sentences.en: So, when I've been in that situation, I don't feel very endeared to the person.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己刚刚被告知我犯了个错误，这让我感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: I feel like I've just been told I made a mistake and I feel bad about it.
sentences.zh: 所以具有讽刺意味的是，是的，我向她传达“我在乎你，我不会做伤害你的事”的愿望，然后，为了不被指责这样做，

sentences.en: So, the irony is, yes, my desire to communicate to her, I care about you and I would not do something to hurt you, I then, in a desire to not be accused of that,
sentences.zh: 我做了一件不必要的事情，而且绝对没有达到让我显得超级关怀和温暖的效果。

sentences.en: I did something that was unnecessary and certainly didn't have the effect of making me show up as super caring and warm.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，你的保姆不会觉得，你知道的，艾莉森是如此、如此聪明能干，而且总是照顾我。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, your nanny is not thinking, you know, Alison is so, so smart and so competent and is always looking out for me.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她会想，为什么艾莉森有这种强迫性的需求来向我证明她是正确的？

sentences.en: You know, she's thinking, why does Alison have this obsessive need to prove to me that she's right?
sentences.zh: 她可能会这么想。

sentences.en: She might be thinking that.
sentences.zh: 我只是，还是那句话，我不会去问她，因为我就是不，我没有做好心理准备去听答案。

sentences.en: I'm just, again, I'm not going to ask her because I just don't, I'm not psychologically prepared to hear the answer.
sentences.zh: 但确实，你遇到了这种情况，这开始显得合乎逻辑了，对吧？

sentences.en: But exactly, you have this, it starts to seem logical, right?
sentences.zh: 我被指责犯了错误。

sentences.en: I've been accused of making a mistake.
sentences.zh: 我必须澄清事实，证明我没有犯错。

sentences.en: I must correct the record that I didn't make a mistake.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种非常自然的倾向会说，哦，这说得通。

sentences.en: There's a pretty natural tendency to say, oh, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这能够挽救声誉。

sentences.en: That's going to be reputation saving.
sentences.zh: 但当你这样做时，我认为在某些情况下，澄清事实绝对是非常重要的。

sentences.en: But then when you do this, you, I think there are some situations where absolutely correcting the record could be really important.
sentences.zh: 我想对我来说，我能够从自己的行为中观察到的是，每当有人说“艾莉森，你可能是错的”时，我都会有一种膝跳反射般的反应。

sentences.en: I think for me, what I've been able to observe about my own behavior is I have a knee-jerk reaction to anytime somebody says, Alison, you might be wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果我真的认为我是对的，我就必须把那个信息亮出来。

sentences.en: If I really do think I'm right to have to put that information out there.
sentences.zh: 我不仅能举出这个例子，还能举出其他例子，在那样做的过程中，我可能对自己的声誉造成了更多的损害。

sentences.en: And I can come up with not just this example, but others where in the act of doing that, I'm probably doing more harm to my reputation.
sentences.zh: 因为即使你没有被指责，你也得把那个信息塞进去，上面写着：为了让你知道，我把每件事都做对了。

sentences.en: Because even when you're not being accused, you got to put in that information that says, just so you know, I was doing everything right.
sentences.zh: 我们还有另一种试图给别人留下印象的方式。

sentences.en: There's another way we try to make an impression on others.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，你最近写了一本书，你写了一个非常有趣的致谢，你的编辑对它有一些想法。

sentences.en: You recently wrote a book, Alison, and you wrote a very interesting dedication that your editor had some thoughts about.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，你最近写了一本书，而且你写了一个非常有意思的题献，你的编辑对此有一些看法。

sentences.en: What did you write and what was your editor's feedback?
sentences.zh: 你写了什么？你编辑的反馈是什么？

sentences.en: So in the first full version of the manuscript that I sent to the editor, the whole thing's done, and the dedication, I wrote it last, and I was actually quite proud of it.
sentences.zh: 所以在发给编辑的第一个完整版手稿里，整本书都写完了，题献我最后才写，而且我其实挺为它自豪的。

sentences.en: This is what I wrote.
sentences.zh: 这就是我写的内容。

sentences.en: So I said, to those who've had to deal with me when I was neither likable nor badass, especially my husband and kids, who often get the worst of me and love me anyway,
sentences.zh: 我说：谨以此书献给那些在我既不可爱也算不上女强人时，仍不得不与我打交道的人，尤其是我的丈夫和孩子们，他们常常承受我最糟糕的一面，却依然爱我；

sentences.en: anyone who knew me in high school, and those unfortunate enough to talk to me before I've had three cups of coffee.
sentences.zh: 献给高中时认识我的人，以及那些在我喝完第三杯咖啡之前，不幸跟我说过话的人。

sentences.en: That was my dedication.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的题献。

sentences.en: And her response was, no, you cannot do this.
sentences.zh: 她的回应是，不行，你不能这么写。

sentences.en: It is way too self-deprecating.
sentences.zh: 这实在是太妄自菲薄了。

sentences.en: You are writing a book to people who do not know you.
sentences.zh: 你写这本书是给不认识你的人看的。

sentences.en: You cannot start off knocking yourself down on page two of this book.
sentences.zh: 你不能在这本书的第二页就开始贬低自己。

sentences.en: So we talked earlier about how you don't like to tell people you went to Dartmouth and Stanford, and it feels like this example is cut from the same cloth.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之前聊过，你不太喜欢告诉别人你去了达特茅斯和斯坦福，感觉这个例子和那种心态如出一辙。

sentences.en: Self-deprecation is all about wanting to come across as humble, but often people don't see our behavior that way.
sentences.zh: 妄自菲薄的本质是想显得谦虚，但人们往往不会那样看待我们的行为。

sentences.en: What happens when we act and talk in self-deprecating ways, Alison?
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，当我们表现出妄自菲薄的行为和言语时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so when I fail to mention I'm where I went to school, it's self-deprecation of omission, but then this dedication is a commission.
sentences.zh: 对，所以当我没有主动提及我在哪所学校上学时，这是一种通过隐瞒来进行的妄自菲薄，但这篇题献是主动为之的。

sentences.en: I'm actually putting information out there in the world voluntarily to say, hey, look at how not good at various things I am.
sentences.zh: 我其实是在自愿向世界输出这样一种信息：嘿，看我在各种事情上有多不行。

sentences.en: And so self-deprecation is a form of humor.
sentences.zh: 所以妄自菲薄是一种幽默的形式。

sentences.en: So one of the reasons that people use it is to be funny.
sentences.zh: 人们使用它原因之一就是为了搞笑。

sentences.en: And humor is a good behavior to put out in the world for our own reputation.
sentences.zh: 而幽默是对我们自身声誉很有帮助的一种行为表现。

sentences.en: It creates social cohesion.
sentences.zh: 它能创造社会凝聚力。

sentences.en: Humor is an intelligent act.
sentences.zh: 幽默是一种智力行为。

sentences.en: If it lands well, it's considered you're considered smarter.
sentences.zh: 如果效果好，你会被人认为更聪明。

sentences.en: So, you know, a lot of comedians that have their whole careers are just poking fun of themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，很多喜剧演员整个职业生涯都在拿自己开涮。

sentences.en: So self-deprecation can be humorous.
sentences.zh: 因此，妄自菲薄是可以很有趣的。

sentences.en: And I think part of the reason I have come to use it is partly that because I have a humorous style and so it fits in with my forms of joke telling.
sentences.zh: 我想我之所以开始使用这种方式，部分原因是我本身就有一种幽默风格，所以这很符合我讲笑话的形式。

sentences.en: The challenge with it is why it's not as good of a form of humor as other things is that people believe what we say about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 它面临的挑战，以及为什么它不如其他幽默形式那么好的原因在于，人们会相信我们对自己的评价。

sentences.en: We are the experts on ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们自己才是关于我们自身的专家。

sentences.en: So if I tell you I'm not very good at something and we see this when people make fun of their looks, they make fun of their intelligence, people see them as less funny,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我告诉你我不擅长某事，而且我们发现当人们取笑自己的长相、取笑自己的智力时，别人就会觉得他们没那么搞笑，

sentences.en: as less good looking, as less intelligent.
sentences.zh: 没那么好看，也没那么聪明。

sentences.en: So we're the experts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们自己才是专家。

sentences.en: So we put ourselves down.
sentences.zh: 因此当我们贬低自己时，

sentences.en: What ends up happening is people say, oh, you just told me you're not very good at that.
sentences.zh: 最终发生的情况是，人们会说，哦，你刚刚告诉我你不太擅长那个。

sentences.en: You must not be very good at it.
sentences.zh: 那你肯定真的很不擅长。

sentences.en: So any benefit you might get from the social cohesion, oh, that's modest, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 所以，你从社会凝聚力中获得的任何好处——哦，这人真谦虚，真不错，

sentences.en: You're taking that corresponding hit by telling somebody you're not very competent or skilled in whatever you just put yourself down on.
sentences.zh: 都会大打折扣，因为你告诉别人你在自己刚刚贬低的事情上能力或技能不足。

sentences.en: There's also the point that if you're good at something, if you've won something and you're trying to, you know, appease someone who has not won something, you know,
sentences.zh: 还有一点就是，如果你很擅长某事，如果你赢得了什么奖项，而你试图去安抚一个没有获奖的人，你知道的，

sentences.en: you've won the gold medal in a race.
sentences.zh: 比如你在比赛中赢得了金牌，

sentences.en: And you're trying to appease the person who is not on the medal stand by saying, oh, you know, medals don't count or, you know, winning is not everything.
sentences.zh: 而你试图通过说“哦，奖牌其实不算什么”或者“赢了并不是一切”，来安抚那个没有站在领奖台上的人。

sentences.en: In some ways, that doesn't make you more liked.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这并不会让你更受欢迎。

sentences.en: The person who hasn't won the medal doesn't want to be told that medals don't count.
sentences.zh: 没赢得奖牌的人并不想听到奖牌不算什么这种话。

sentences.en: They're upset about not having won the medal.
sentences.zh: 他们正为没有赢得奖牌而感到难过。

sentences.en: And you was standing on the medal stand telling them that medals don't count.
sentences.zh: 而你却站在领奖台上告诉他们奖牌根本不重要。

sentences.en: It's like the rich person telling the poor person, well, you know, don't really worry about it.
sentences.zh: 这就好比富人对穷人说，嗯，你知道的，别太担心，

sentences.en: Money doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 钱其实真的不重要。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So when people have outperformed others and then they try to downplay their performance, their high performance, it doesn't land well exactly in the way that you describe.
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们的表现优于他人，然后又试图淡化自己的表现、他们的高水准表现时，效果往往不佳，正如你所描述的那样。

sentences.en: People say, I don't believe you, one.
sentences.zh: 人们会说，首先，我不相信你。

sentences.en: So now you're, you know, you're not an honest person.
sentences.zh: 所以现在在别人看来，你是个不诚实的人。

sentences.en: And two, it doesn't make me feel any better.
sentences.zh: 其次，这并没有让我感觉好受一点。

sentences.en: So I don't actually feel connected to you or appreciate what you've done.
sentences.zh: 所以我其实并没有觉得跟你拉近了距离，也不觉得你做的事有多了不起。

sentences.en: We've all done things like this to shape how others perceive us.
sentences.zh: 我们都做过类似的事情来塑造别人对我们的看法。

sentences.en: We downplay our accomplishments to seem humble.
sentences.zh: 我们淡化自己的成就来显得谦虚。

sentences.en: We belabor a point to appear intelligent.
sentences.zh: 我们喋喋不休地阐述一个观点来显得聪明。

sentences.en: There are certain traits we all want to be known for.
sentences.zh: 我们都希望自己拥有某些特定的特质并以此闻名。

sentences.en: Allison's research puts these traits into two distinct categories.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森的研究将这些特质分成了两个截然不同的维度。

sentences.en: Yeah, so these are the two fundamental dimensions of person perception.
sentences.zh: 对，这些是人际知觉的两个基本维度。

sentences.en: Some different people call them different names, but you're going to have a dimension of assertiveness.
sentences.zh: 不同的人对它们的称呼可能不同，但其中一个维度是果断性。

sentences.en: Can you get stuff done?
sentences.zh: 你能把事情办成吗？

sentences.en: It's going to be decisive and persistent and competent.
sentences.zh: 它关乎果断、执着和能力。

sentences.en: And then a dimension of warmth.
sentences.zh: 另一个维度是热情。

sentences.en: Do you care about people other than yourself?
sentences.zh: 除了你自己之外，你还在乎别人吗？

sentences.en: And these are very much linked to status.
sentences.zh: 这些与地位息息相关。

sentences.en: So when we think about people we respect, we respect people who are assertive and they can get tasks done well and effectively.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们想到我们尊重的人时，我们尊重那些果断、能够出色且高效完成任务的人。

sentences.en: And we respect people who care about people other than themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们也尊重那些关心自己以外的人的人。

sentences.en: Those are two fundamental dimensions of person perception.
sentences.zh: 这就是人际知觉的两个基本维度。

sentences.en: When we pay attention to people and what they're doing, we code their behavior along those two dimensions.
sentences.zh: 当我们关注他人及其行为时，我们会沿着这两个维度对他们的行为进行归类编码。

sentences.en: And they're very much tied to this idea of status.
sentences.zh: 它们与地位这个概念紧密相连。

sentences.en: And there can be attention because you can think about it as a two-dimensional space.
sentences.zh: 这里面可能会产生一种张力，因为你可以把它想象成一个二维空间。

sentences.en: So you can be high on one dimension, low on the other.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在一个维度上得分很高，而在另一个维度上得分很低。

sentences.en: So you can think about doing things that get you a lot of credit for being assertive and competent and decisive, but are seen as less warm.
sentences.zh: 你可以去做那些能为你赢得很多果断、能力和决断力赞誉的事情，但这些事情会被认为缺乏热情。

sentences.en: And you can think of situations where you can do things that are going to help you be seen as really nice and kind and likable,
sentences.zh: 你也可以想象这样一些情境：你做的事情能帮你树立非常亲切、友好和讨人喜欢的形象，

sentences.en: but often at the expense of your own competence and capabilities.
sentences.zh: 但往往是以牺牲你自己的能力和才干为代价的。

sentences.en: And so that's where the tension exists is because there are two cells that people will find themselves, I found myself in, many, many times in life where you're getting one,
sentences.zh: 所以张力就是这样产生的，因为人们在生活中会发现自己很多很多次陷入这样两个象限中：你得到了其中一个，

sentences.en: but you're not getting the other.
sentences.zh: 却失去了另一个。

sentences.en: Allison has found in her research that people can be rated low on both assertiveness and on warmth.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森在研究中发现，人们在果断性和热情这两个维度上都可能被评得很低。

sentences.en: We don't respect people who are selfish and lack confidence.
sentences.zh: 我们不尊重那些自私且缺乏自信的人。

sentences.en: By contrast, everyone respects people who are seen as both assertive and kind.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，所有人都尊重那些既果断又善良的人。

sentences.en: The most beloved leaders in history invariably combine both qualities.
sentences.zh: 历史上最受爱戴的领导人无一例外地兼具这两种品质。

sentences.en: That's the quadrant we should all aspire to inhabit.
sentences.zh: 那是我们所有人都应该渴望进驻的象限。

sentences.en: But you can also be rated high on one dimension and low on the other.
sentences.zh: 但你也有可能在一个维度上得分很高，而在另一个维度上得分很低。

sentences.en: A ruthless hedge fund manager might be rated very high on competence and assertiveness, but be widely perceived as a jerk.
sentences.zh: 一个冷酷无情的对冲基金经理在能力和果断性上的评分可能非常高，但普遍会被人觉得是个混蛋。

sentences.en: Or you can have people who are seen as sweet, but ineffectual.
sentences.zh: 或者你也会遇到这样的人，他们被认为人很好，但却无所作为、毫无建树。

sentences.en: To complicate matters, these two dimensions are sometimes at odds with one another.
sentences.zh: 更复杂的是，这两个维度有时甚至是相互矛盾的。

sentences.en: To be seen as assertive can make you less likely to be seen as warm and kind, especially if you're a woman.
sentences.zh: 表现得果断可能会降低你被视为热情和善良的可能性，特别是如果你是个女性的话。

sentences.en: Women are stereotypically expected to be kind and sweet, so if a woman shows up in a meeting as very assertive, people unconsciously assume she cannot be nice.
sentences.zh: 社会对女性的刻板印象是应该善良和甜美，所以如果一个女性在会议表现得非常果断，人们会不自觉地认为她不可能是个好人。

sentences.en: The researcher Jennifer Chapman once conducted a study looking at the teaching evaluations of male and female professors.
sentences.zh: 研究员詹妮弗·查普曼曾做过一项研究，考察男女教授的教学评估。

sentences.en: I thought this was an amazing and depressing study as a middle-aged professor myself.
sentences.zh: 作为一名中年教授，我当时觉得这项研究既精彩又让人沮丧。

sentences.en: What Jennifer and her colleagues did was they looked at longitudinal data of 15 years about of professors teaching evaluations.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗和她的同事们查阅了长达15年的教授教学评估纵向数据。

sentences.en: So they would have the same person like me, who's taught for 20 years, show up multiple times.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会追踪像我这样教龄20年的人，在不同时间多次出现的数据。

sentences.en: They've taught years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 他们教了整整一年又一年。

sentences.en: And they would compare each individual to themselves to say, okay, how did your evaluations change over time?
sentences.zh: 他们会将每个人自身进行纵向对比，来看看：好吧，随着时间推移，你的评估结果发生了怎样的变化？

sentences.en: And you might think, oh, evaluations are going to get better for the people who succeed and stay because they'll become more experienced professors.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，哦，对于那些成功留下来的人来说，教学评估应该会变得越来越好，因为他们成了更有经验的教授。

sentences.en: And then, I don't know, maybe at the end of their career, they tail off and they get worse.
sentences.zh: 然后，我不知道，也许在他们职业生涯的末期，教学评估会下滑并变差。

sentences.en: But what she and her colleagues found was this curve for female professors only.
sentences.zh: 但她和同事们发现，这种曲线只出现在女教授身上。

sentences.en: When they were younger, they would get high evaluations.
sentences.zh: 当她们年轻时，会获得很高的教学评估。

sentences.en: As they went into middle age, their evaluations would drop.
sentences.zh: 当她们进入中年时，评估就会下降。

sentences.en: And as they got older, their evaluations would rise again.
sentences.zh: 而当她们变老时，评估又会再次上升。

sentences.en: And that pattern was only observed for women, and it was not observed for the male faculty.
sentences.zh: 这种规律只在女性身上观察到，而在男性教员身上并没有出现。

sentences.en: And they did some digging to find support for their theory, which relates to these dimensions of assertiveness and warmth,
sentences.zh: 为了替她们的理论寻找支撑，她们做了一些深入挖掘，这与果断性和热情这两个维度有关，

sentences.en: which is that the women who got the lowest teaching evaluations, which remember the women at the middle age, middle stage of their career,
sentences.zh: 即那些获得最低教学评估的女性——请记住，也就是处于职业生涯中期的女性——

sentences.en: those women were perceived as the most assertive and the least warm.
sentences.zh: 这些女性被认为是最果断但最不热情的。

sentences.en: And that pattern of your assertive and cold was the unique perception of the middle-aged women in the faculty, but not for the men.
sentences.zh: 而这种“你很果断却很冷漠”的模式，是人们对教员中中年女性的独特看法，对男性则没有。

sentences.en: And that research is very consistent with the work that I've done, which is that when are women going to be at their highest power in their academic career?
sentences.zh: 这项研究与我所做的工作非常一致，那就是：女性在学术生涯中何时能达到权力的巅峰？

sentences.en: Generally, generally at that midpoint, that's when you are tenured, you're serving in major administrative roles, etc.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，通常是在那个中点，也就是你获得终身教职、担任重要行政职务等等的时候。

sentences.en: And so the story that I could tell from that study is, okay, if your power increases and your status doesn't, guess where you end up?
sentences.zh: 所以，我可以从那项研究中得出的故事是，好吧，如果你的权力增长了，而你的地位没有同步增长，猜猜你会落入什么境地？

sentences.en: In the low-status power holder cell, which is very assertive and very cold.
sentences.zh: 落入“低地位的权力掌控者”象限，也就是非常果断且非常冷漠。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 结果呢？

sentences.en: People don't like it, and they don't treat you very well.
sentences.zh: 人们不喜欢这样，对你的态度也不会好。

sentences.en: And in this case, the mistreatment came in the form of the lower teaching evaluations, the lower performance evaluations that the female faculty got.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这种恶劣对待表现为女教员们获得的教学评估更低、绩效评估也更低。

sentences.en: When women acquire power in the workplace, a number of studies have found they are less likely to be perceived as warm and nice.
sentences.zh: 多项研究发现，当女性在职场中获得权力时，她们被视为热情和亲切的可能性往往会降低。

sentences.en: They are seen as powerful, but cruel.
sentences.zh: 她们会被视为有权有势，但也很残酷。

sentences.en: Allison says that combination makes us afraid.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森说，这种组合让人感到害怕。

sentences.en: Because if someone's going to have control over me, I care a lot about the fact that they are going to do good things with it,
sentences.zh: 因为如果有人要对我有控制权，我非常在乎他们是否会用这种权力做好事，

sentences.en: not just to help me, but to make sure they're going to use it responsibly.
sentences.zh: 不仅是为了帮助我，还要确保他们会负责任地使用它。

sentences.en: And if I don't respect somebody, I could be concerned, wait a second, you're going to have all this control, and you're just going to mess it up.
sentences.zh: 如果我不尊重某个人，我就会担心，等一下，你要掌握这么大的控制权，结果却把它搞砸。

sentences.en: From friendships to job promotions, there are many consequences to how we go about interacting with others.
sentences.zh: 从友谊到工作晋升，我们与他人互动的方式会带来诸多后果。

sentences.en: Despite the great deal of time and effort we spend in managing how others see us, our efforts often backfire,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们花了很多时间和精力来经营别人眼中的自己，但我们的努力往往适得其反，

sentences.en: and people don't come away thinking of us as warm, competent, and humble people.
sentences.zh: 人们离开时并不觉得我们是热情、胜任且谦逊的人。

sentences.en: When we come back, better ways to win friends and influence people.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，我们将探讨赢得朋友和影响他人的更好方法。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐蔽大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐蔽大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: We spend a lot of time and effort trying to paint a certain picture of ourselves in other people's eyes.
sentences.zh: 我们花了大量时间和精力，试图在别人眼中勾勒出自己的某种特定形象。

sentences.en: Organizational psychologist Alison Fregale is the author of Likeable Badass, How Women Get the Success They Deserve.
sentences.zh: 组织心理学家艾莉森·弗雷加尔是《讨人喜欢的女强人：女性如何获得应得的成功》一书的作者。

sentences.en: She says that when we try to burnish our status, many of us use the wrong brush.
sentences.zh: 她说，当我们试图提升自己的地位时，我们很多人都用错了刷子。

sentences.en: Alison, we've been talking about status, how much we're respected, admired, and valued in the eyes of others,
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，我们一直在讨论地位，也就是我们在别人眼中的受尊重、被崇拜和被重视程度，

sentences.en: and the wrong ways we often go about trying to build our status.
sentences.zh: 以及我们为了建立地位而经常采用的错误方法。

sentences.en: A lot of people believe that you have this trade-off.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为，你必须做出某种权衡取舍。

sentences.en: Either I come across as assertive, or I come across as warm.
sentences.zh: 要么我表现得很果断，要么我表现得很热情。

sentences.en: Or I come across as really likable, but then I sacrifice being seen as competent.
sentences.zh: 或者我表现得非常讨人喜欢，但为此牺牲了自己被视为有能力的形象。

sentences.en: You say that being successful involves eliminating this trade-off and coming across as both assertive and warm?
sentences.zh: 你却说，成功需要消除这种权衡，做到既果断又热情？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So, status is how much we're respected and regarded.
sentences.zh: 所以，地位就是我们受尊重和被推崇的程度。

sentences.en: It's critically important to our life satisfaction and our career success.
sentences.zh: 它对我们的生活满意度和职业成功至关重要。

sentences.en: It's a fundamental human need.
sentences.zh: 这是人类的一项基本需求。

sentences.en: Lacking status is physically and psychologically as damaging as living a life without friends.
sentences.zh: 缺乏地位在生理和心理上造成的损害，不亚于过着没有朋友的生活。

sentences.en: So, building status is critical.
sentences.zh: 因此，建立地位至关重要。

sentences.en: How do we do it?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么做？

sentences.en: We do it by showing up as assertive and warm.
sentences.zh: 我们通过展现果断与热情来做到这一点。

sentences.en: There's no doubt that for some people, women included, that getting to that quadrant feels elusive.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，对某些人（包括女性）来说，要达到那个象限感觉遥不可及。

sentences.en: But what I help people think about is it doesn't have to be elusive.
sentences.zh: 但我帮助人们思考的是，它其实并不一定遥不可及。

sentences.en: And the first step in making it work, in getting to that quadrant, is not unintentionally doing things that are going to put you somewhere else in that two-dimensional space.
sentences.zh: 实现这一目标、进入那个象限的第一步，就是不要无意中做出那些会把你推向二维空间其他位置的事情。

sentences.en: And there's a phenomenon in psychology known as compensatory impression management.
sentences.zh: 心理学上有一个现象叫做“补偿性印象管理”。

sentences.en: And that's the tendency that human beings have, not just women, but human beings, that when you want to show up as really strong on one of those dimensions, you do it in a bad way.
sentences.zh: 这是人类（不仅仅是女性，而是整个人类）的一种倾向：当你想要在其中一个维度上表现得非常强势时，你往往会用一种糟糕的方式去做。

sentences.en: You do it by making yourself look worse on the other.
sentences.zh: 你通过让自己在另一个维度上看起来更糟来做到这一点。

sentences.en: You want to show up as really assertive.
sentences.zh: 你想表现得非常果断。

sentences.en: You do it by showing up as less warm, which makes no sense.
sentences.zh: 你采取的方法是表现得不那么热情，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: If you want to show up as assertive, you should show up as assertive.
sentences.zh: 如果你想表现得果断，你就应该直接表现得果断。

sentences.en: That's not what people do.
sentences.zh: 但人们并不是这么做的。

sentences.en: They say, I want to be really assertive, so I'm going to be less warm.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我想变得非常果断，所以我要表现得不那么热情。

sentences.en: I want to be really warm, so now I'm going to be less assertive.
sentences.zh: 我想表现得非常热情，所以现在我要稍微减少一点强势。

sentences.en: And that's we compensate when we don't have to.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我们在不需要的时候反而会去做的过度补偿。

sentences.en: So that quadrant, assertive and warm, it's possible to get there.
sentences.zh: 所以那个象限，既强势又热情，是完全有可能达到的。

sentences.en: It can be harder for some people.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说可能更难一些。

sentences.en: But we also make it harder on ourselves than it has to be by engaging in behaviors where we're deliberately only showcasing one and not the other,
sentences.zh: 但我们往往会故意表现得只具备其中一种特质，而不是两种兼顾，从而人为地增加了达成目标的难度，

sentences.en: when that is a false choice that doesn't have to be made.
sentences.zh: 而这其实是一个完全没必要去做的伪命题。

sentences.en: And so one of the things I help people think about when they're thinking about how can I show up in this assertive and warm cell is I say, start with what,
sentences.zh: 因此，当人们在思考“我该如何在既强势又热情的象限中展现自己”时，我帮大家梳理的其中一个方法就是：从……开始，

sentences.en: who you naturally are and then add, don't subtract.
sentences.zh: 从你本来的样子开始，然后做加法，而不是减法。

sentences.en: So if you have something that's very natural and authentic to you, even if it's more submissive, like your speech style, or maybe if it's not as friendly,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你身上有什么非常自然且真实的特质，哪怕它偏向顺从，比如你的说话风格，或者可能不够友好，

sentences.en: like you're not a great smiler, okay, fine, it is what it is.
sentences.zh: 比如你不太擅长微笑，好吧，没关系，事实就是这样。

sentences.en: But what are the things that you can add in that are going to get you more recognition on the other dimension where you think you might be lacking?
sentences.zh: 但你可以加入哪些特质，来为你自认为可能有所欠缺的另一个维度赢得更多认可呢？

sentences.en: So, Alison, you say that one of the ways we can try and get the best of both these worlds is to try and offer help to other people.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，你提到过，我们试图兼顾这两个世界的一种方法是尝试向他人提供帮助。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, helping another person is definitely a warm act, it's a giving act, it's in service to somebody else.
sentences.zh: 嗯，帮助他人绝对是一种热情的行为，一种付出的行为，是在为他人服务。

sentences.en: And if the help that you're offering also showcases that you are highly capable, then you can, in the act of helping, get credit for assertiveness as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你提供的帮助同时也展现出你能力非凡，那么你在伸出援手的同时，也能为自己的强势赢得赞赏。

sentences.en: So if a friend needs a ride to the airport and I drive them, very warm thing to do, not particularly assertive, everybody else can drive to the airport as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果朋友需要搭便车去机场而我开车送了他，这是一件非常热情的事，但谈不上多强势，因为其他人也都能开车去机场。

sentences.en: It doesn't help me show up as very unique or talented in any way.
sentences.zh: 这并没有帮我以任何独特或有才华的方式脱颖而出。

sentences.en: But if I have something that I do have a unique contribution, I always pride myself on being a good childcare evaluator and hirer.
sentences.zh: 但如果我有自己独特的贡献，我一直为自己能成为一个出色的育儿嫂评估员和招聘者而感到自豪。

sentences.en: I could not do my work without the support of a lot of people in my life who take great care of my kids.
sentences.zh: 如果生活中没有许多人的支持，没有他们把我孩子照顾得井井有条，我根本无法完成工作。

sentences.en: And I feel over the years, I've gotten really good at finding great people, setting up the expectations of the relationship very well,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这些年来，我在寻找优秀人才、明确双方关系期望方面变得非常擅长，

sentences.en: and creating a good environment for them to work in that has really been very successful.
sentences.zh: 并为他们创造了一个良好的工作环境，这确实取得了极大的成功。

sentences.en: And when I see other people struggling, other parents, I'm quick to jump in and offer some advice or help, because it's unique.
sentences.zh: 每当我看到别人——其他父母在挣扎时，我总是迅速介入并提供一些建议或帮助，因为这是我独一无二的优势。

sentences.en: It's something that I can offer that another person couldn't easily offer just at that moment.
sentences.zh: 这是我在那个特定时刻能够提供，而别人无法轻易提供的东西。

sentences.en: And so when we help in big or small ways that showcase our talents and give assistance to other people,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们以展现自身才能并为他人提供协助的大事小情去施以援手时，

sentences.en: that's an example of something that gets you credit for the assertiveness and credit for the warmth.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个既能为你赢得强势认可又能为你赢得热情认可的例子。

sentences.en: Allison says another way to come across as both assertive and warm has to do with how we respond to praise and how we engage in self-promotion.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森说，另一种展现既强势又热情的方法，与我们如何回应赞美以及如何进行自我宣传有关。

sentences.en: A lot of information that people know about you, it ultimately originates with you.
sentences.zh: 人们对你的很多了解，归根结底都源于你自己。

sentences.en: It's either interactions they've had with you, it's information you've put out into social media or on a website, something like that.
sentences.zh: 要么是他们与你的互动，要么是你发布在社交媒体或网站上的信息，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so we control a lot of the information that people get about us.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们掌控着别人获得的关于我们的很大一部分信息。

sentences.en: So we want to make that information certainly as positive as possible on both dimensions, right, on assertive and warm.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望确保这些信息在两个维度上都尽可能积极，对吧，既强势又热情。

sentences.en: So there was some research that I thought was great that supported a technique that I had adopted myself years and years ago.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究我觉得非常棒，它支持了我多年前采用的一种方法。

sentences.en: And I call it brag and thank, and the psychologist who looked at it called it dual promotion or promoting self and other people at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我把它叫做“吹嘘与感谢”，而研究过这一现象的心理学家称之为“双重宣传”，即同时宣传自己和他人。

sentences.en: So when we promote ourselves and we say something good, we can imagine we're going to get an assertiveness bump, but oh, maybe it's not so modeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们宣传自己并说出一些好话时，我们可以想象，我们的强势形象会得到提升，但哦，这或许不够谦逊。

sentences.en: So now we get a warm hit.
sentences.zh: 于是我们的热情分值就受到了打击。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 那么，

sentences.en: what if you also at the same time are offering sincere promotion and praise for somebody else who did something great in the process without diminishing or self-deprecating what you did,
sentences.zh: 如果在这样做的同时，你也对在这个过程中做出杰出贡献的其他人给予了真诚的宣传和赞美，而又没有贬低或自嘲你所做的事情，

sentences.en: but to say, hey, I had this great success, right?
sentences.zh: 而是说：嘿，我取得了这个巨大的成功，对吧？

sentences.en: I got to, you know, achieve something and special thanks go to people A, B and C without whom this could never happen.
sentences.zh: 我得以（你知道的）达成了一些成就，特别感谢A、B、C三位，没有他们这一切绝无可能实现。

sentences.en: So you're telling your story, but you're at the same time saying something positive about other people.
sentences.zh: 所以你在讲述自己的故事，但与此同时你也在说关于其他人的好话。

sentences.en: That's an example of where you can use something that we've been told to do, self-promote and tweak it, just add to it in a way that's promoting the other people.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个例子，你可以采用我们常被告知要做的事情——自我宣传，并对其进行微调，加入赞美他人的内容。

sentences.en: You get more credit for the warmth.
sentences.zh: 你会为自己的热情赢得更多认可。

sentences.en: You talk about another idea called humor bragging that could help us in some ways resolve this tension between coming across as assertive and coming across as warm.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了另一个名为“幽默自吹”的想法，它在某些方面可以帮助我们化解“表现得强势”与“表现得热情”之间的这种张力。

sentences.en: What is humor bragging, Alison?
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，什么是幽默自吹？

sentences.en: So humor bragging is saying something positive about yourself while also using humor that is not self-deprecating.
sentences.zh: 所以幽默自吹就是说一些关于自己的积极事情，同时使用不带有自嘲性质的幽默。

sentences.en: And this is one of my favorite findings that just recently came out, and I think it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这是我最近看到的最喜欢的发现之一，我认为它太妙了。

sentences.en: And what the research team found was that when people in a context where you might need to self-promote or brag, like searching for a job,
sentences.zh: 研究团队发现，当人们在需要自我宣传或吹嘘的情境下（比如找工作），

sentences.en: where somebody said something positive and then added in something humorous,
sentences.zh: 如果有人说了积极的话然后又加入了一些幽默元素，

sentences.en: those people were granted more status and were more likely to be seen as viable candidates in a job selection process, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如在工作甄选过程中，这些人会被赋予更高的地位，并更有可能被视为切实可行的候选人。

sentences.en: One of the examples they had in the study was a job applicant who wrote a purely self-promoting statement that said,
sentences.zh: 研究中的其中一个例子是一名求职者写了一份纯粹自我宣传的声明，上面写着：

sentences.en: I'm highly motivated and detail-oriented sales representative with experience and a proven track record of people skills.
sentences.zh: 我是一位高度积极且注重细节的销售代表，拥有丰富的经验以及经证明的人际交往能力记录。

sentences.en: I look forward to supporting your company's goals dedicatedly.
sentences.zh: 我期待着全力支持贵公司的目标。

sentences.en: And then in another version offered a humor bragging statement.
sentences.zh: 而在另一个版本中，则提供了一份幽默自吹的声明。

sentences.en: I'm a driven sales representative who's detail-oriented and passionate about serving your company's goals.
sentences.zh: 我是一位充满干劲的销售代表，注重细节，热衷于服务贵公司的目标。

sentences.en: I have a proven track record of turning caffeine input into productivity output.
sentences.zh: 我拥有将咖啡输入转化为生产力输出的辉煌战绩。

sentences.en: The more coffee you can provide, the more output I will produce.
sentences.zh: 你们提供的咖啡越多，我产出的成果就越多。

sentences.en: And they found that when it was, again, a positive statement combined with some humor, there was more interest in the candidate.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，当积极的陈述再次与幽默相结合时，人们对候选人的兴趣就更高了。

sentences.en: The candidate did a better job building their status and being able to be seen as a viable candidate for the job.
sentences.zh: 这位候选人在建立自身地位以及被视为该职位的可行候选人方面做得更好。

sentences.en: That's what humor bragging is.
sentences.zh: 这就是幽默自吹。

sentences.en: So you've talked about how we sometimes hide our successes in order to come across as more warm and more likable.
sentences.zh: 所以你讨论了我们有时如何隐藏自己的成功，以便显得更加热情、更加招人喜爱。

sentences.en: So when we think our accomplishments will intimidate someone else, we sometimes mistakenly downplay them.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们认为自己的成就可能会吓到别人时，我们有时会错误地将其淡化。

sentences.en: You say that if someone is worried about coming across as intimidating,
sentences.zh: 你说过，如果有人担心自己显得令人生畏，

sentences.en: one way to buffer against that is to highlight their similarities with others.
sentences.zh: 抵御这种担忧的方法之一就是突出他们与他人的共同点。

sentences.en: And you have a friend named Greg who exemplifies this strategy.
sentences.zh: 你有一位名叫格雷格的朋友，他就是这种策略的典范。

sentences.en: What does Greg do?
sentences.zh: 格雷格做了什么？

sentences.en: So Greg Northcraft, co-author of mine, former colleague, long-time professor at the University of Illinois, who is now retired.
sentences.zh: 所以格雷格·诺斯克拉夫特，我的合著者、前同事、伊利诺伊大学的长期教授，现在已经退休了。

sentences.en: And what I think Greg does now the most is play a tremendous amount of golf after he moved to California.
sentences.zh: 而我认为格雷格现在做得最多的事，就是在搬到加州后打了大量的尔夫球。

sentences.en: So he's an incredibly avid golfer, and everyone who knows him knows that.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个狂热的高尔夫球手，每个认识他的人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: In fact, his strategy for showing up as assertive and warm really relied on golf.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他表现得既强势又热情的策略确实依赖于高尔夫。

sentences.en: And what he understood as a psychologist was he understood similarity attraction.
sentences.zh: 作为一名心理学家，他所理解的是“相似吸引效应”。

sentences.en: The greatest basis of liking and attraction that psychology has ever documented is similarity.
sentences.zh: 心理学有史以来记录在案的好感和吸引力的基础就是相似性。

sentences.en: We like people who are like us.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢和我们相似的人。

sentences.en: And because we think positive things about ourselves, someone who's like us is very likely to get respect because what a brilliant and loving person that person is.
sentences.zh: 由于我们对自己的看法很积极，一个像我们的人极有可能赢得尊重，因为这个人是多么聪明和充满爱心啊。

sentences.en: So what Greg always told me is he said, the first thing I always try to do whenever I'm talking to a new person is figure out if there's any chance they like golf.
sentences.zh: 所以格雷格总是告诉我，他说，每当我跟一个新认识的人交谈时，我首先要做的就是弄清楚他们有没有可能喜欢高尔夫。

sentences.en: Does that logo on their shirt represent a golf course?
sentences.zh: 他们衬衫上的那个标志代表的是高尔夫球场吗？

sentences.en: I wouldn't know because I don't golf, but Greg did.
sentences.zh: 我可不知道，因为我不打高尔夫，但格雷格知道。

sentences.en: And if he saw any opportunity to bring golf into the conversation, he would.
sentences.zh: 如果他看到任何把高尔夫扯进对话的机会，他都会这么做。

sentences.en: And he told me a story once about his biggest win, which was talking to somebody else at the university.
sentences.zh: 他曾向我讲述过他的一次最大胜绩，那就是与大学里的另一个人交谈。

sentences.en: They didn't know each other.
sentences.zh: 他们并不认识对方。

sentences.en: And the subject of the conversation was probably money, but some scarce resource where you have every reason to think it's going to be a bit of a territorial battle.
sentences.zh: 谈话的主题可能是金钱，但总之是一些稀缺资源，让你有充分的理由认为这将会是一场带有领地意识的争夺战。

sentences.en: But he did something deliberate.
sentences.zh: 但他做了一件刻意为之的事。

sentences.en: He said, I had the status to ask this person to come to my office.
sentences.zh: 他说，我有身份要求这个人来我的办公室。

sentences.en: Like I had, I was the senior person in this in exchange, but I didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 就像我有，我是这次交流中资历更深的人，但我没有这么做。

sentences.en: I specifically offered to go to the other guy's office for one reason only was I wanted to see his physical space.
sentences.zh: 我特意提出去另一个家伙的办公室，原因只有一个：我想看看他的物理空间。

sentences.en: And so I could figure out what does this guy like, what does he do?
sentences.zh: 这样我才能弄清楚这家伙喜欢什么，他做什么？

sentences.en: How could I make a connection with him?
sentences.zh: 我该如何与他建立联系？

sentences.en: And he went into the office and he said, I couldn't believe my luck.
sentences.zh: 他走办公室说，我简直不敢相信自己的运气。

sentences.en: I go in and what is behind this guy's desk?
sentences.zh: 我走进去，结果在这个家伙的办公桌后面看到了什么？

sentences.en: He tells a story like he's shaking his hand.
sentences.zh: 他讲起这个故事时好像在握手一样。

sentences.en: And as he does it, he's kind of peering over his shoulder trying to see what's there.
sentences.zh: 当他这么做的时候，他一边把头探过肩膀试图看看那里有什么。

sentences.en: And he says, behind the desk, you're not going to believe it.
sentences.zh: 他说，在办公桌后面，你绝对不会相信。

sentences.en: There's a hole in one trophy.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个一杆进洞的奖杯。

sentences.en: And he said, if you're a golfer and you ever see a hole in one trophy, you know, two things are absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果你是个高尔夫球手，而且你见过一杆进洞奖杯，你知道有两件事绝对是真的。

sentences.en: There has to be a heck of a story behind the trophy.
sentences.zh: 奖杯背后一定有一个了不起的故事。

sentences.en: And the person behind the desk is just dying to tell you what it is.
sentences.zh: 办公桌后面的人正渴望把这个故事告诉你。

sentences.en: So he asks with genuine sincerity and intereSt.
sentences.zh: 于是他带着真诚和兴趣发问。

sentences.en: Oh my God, you have a hole in one.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你竟然打出过一杆进洞。

sentences.en: You need to tell me this story.
sentences.zh: 你得把这个故事讲给我听听。

sentences.en: And the guy does.
sentences.zh: 那个人就讲了。

sentences.en: And Greg had had one hole in one in his life up until that point.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，格雷格自己的人生中也只打出过一次一杆进洞。

sentences.en: He shares his hole in one story.
sentences.zh: 他分享了自己的“一杆进洞”故事。

sentences.en: And you know exactly how this goes because we've all been in these situations at times, too.
sentences.zh: 你知道事情接下来会怎么发展，因为我们有时也都经历过这种情境。

sentences.en: Maybe not about golf.
sentences.zh: 也许不是关于高尔夫。

sentences.en: But if 60 minutes are on the calendar for that meeting, 55 minutes are spent talking golf.
sentences.zh: 但如果日历上显示这次会议有60分钟，那么其中55分钟都在聊高尔夫。

sentences.en: And by the end, they're friends.
sentences.zh: 到最后，他们成了朋友。

sentences.en: And so I always say there's a tremendous amount of luck in that story.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是说那个故事里有很大一部分运气。

sentences.en: He did not know when he walked into the office that day he was going to get an avid golfer.
sentences.zh: 他那天走进办公室时并不知道自己会遇到一个狂热的高尔夫球手。

sentences.en: But the part that's not luck is that Greg spent his 30-year career always looking to find genuine points of commonality with people and bringing them up.
sentences.zh: 但并非靠运气的部分在于，格雷格的30年职业生涯一直都在寻找与人们的共同点并将其提出来。

sentences.en: And the scientist in him was able to say, I know that that really is how we influence people and how we can build our status.
sentences.zh: 他身上的科学家特质使他说得出：我知道这确实是我们影响他人以及建立地位的方式。

sentences.en: And so the golf had nothing to do with whatever money discussion they were going to have.
sentences.zh: 所以高尔夫与他们要讨论的任何金钱话题都毫无关系。

sentences.en: But it built that rapport.
sentences.zh: 但它建立起了这种融洽的关系。

sentences.en: And that's the part where we can be more intentional about saying to somebody, like, I see you and we have something in common.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们可以更加刻意地对某人说的话，比如，我看到你了，我们有共同点。

sentences.en: And that is an easy tool we can all use to start to build the relationship and build status.
sentences.zh: 这是我们所有人都可以轻松使用的工具，用来开始建立关系并树立地位。

sentences.en: So your point here, Alison, is that in some ways, maybe if you're a woman, maybe if you're a person of color, maybe if you're an elderly person,
sentences.zh: 所以你的观点是，艾莉森，在某些方面，也许如果你是一名女性，也许如果你是有色人种，也许如果你是一位老年人，

sentences.en: you might be seen as different from the get-go.
sentences.zh: 你从一开始就可能会被视为与众不同。

sentences.en: And so the importance of finding similarities in some ways becomes more important because you actually want to show the other person you have a point of connection.
sentences.zh: 因此，寻找相似之处的重要性在某些方面变得更加重要，因为你实际上是想向对方表明你们有相通之处。

sentences.en: There's an element of this that also sounds really unfair because you're asking the person who is being unfairly perceived as being different,
sentences.zh: 这里面还有一点也让人觉得很不公平，因为你要求那个被不公平地视为与众不同的人去这样做，

sentences.en: different because she's a woman, different because you're old, different because of something that's outside of your own power to change.
sentences.zh: 因为她是女性而与众不同，因为你老了而与众不同，因为一些超出你自身掌控能力去改变的事情而与众不同。

sentences.en: You're asking them to do the heavy lifting and the hard work to establish similarity in some ways to compensate for the stereotypes that might be in the mind of the other person.
sentences.zh: 你要求他们去承担繁重的工作和付出艰辛的努力来建立相似性，在某种程度上是为了弥补对方脑海中可能存在的刻板印象。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you for asking that.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢你提出这个问题。

sentences.en: It's something I think about in my work a lot because I do spend a lot of time counseling women and helping them excel,
sentences.zh: 这是我在工作中经常思考的事情，因为我确实花了很多时间为女性提供咨询并帮助她们脱颖而出，

sentences.en: essentially figuring out how to take the rules of an unfair game and succeed anyway.
sentences.zh: 本质上就是找出如何利用一场不公平的游戏的规则却依然取得成功的方法。

sentences.en: And so I admit that there's many things in all of this that are incredibly unfair, but I look at Greg's example, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我承认这里面的许多事情都极其不公平，但我看看格雷格的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: Human beings like people who are like them.
sentences.zh: 人类喜欢和自己相似的人。

sentences.en: That's not a standard that only applies to women, people of color, somebody who lacks an ascribed status characteristic.
sentences.zh: 这并非只适用于女性、有色人种或缺乏某种归属地位特征的人的标准。

sentences.en: Greg is a white man.
sentences.zh: 格雷格是一个白人男性。

sentences.en: He still benefited tremendously in his career from establishing real relationships that started by people saying,
sentences.zh: 他在职业生涯中依然从建立真正的关系中获得了巨大的益处，而这段关系始于人们说：

sentences.en: we have something really in common, but what he did was he went looking for it.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有共同点，而他所做的是他主动去寻找了这些共同点。

sentences.en: So one of the ways that I feel really good about working with women in particular and counseling them on things they can do is that I would give the exact same advice to everybody,
sentences.zh: 因此，我乐于与女性合作并就她们可以做的事情提供咨询的原因之一在于，我会向所有人提供完全相同的建议，

sentences.en: because these are the things we see in psychology are the good things.
sentences.zh: 因为这些都是我们在心理学中看到的行之有效的良方。

sentences.en: The humor bragging, as an example, it could be a great tool to overcome a status disadvantage that you don't deserve,
sentences.zh: 以幽默自吹为例，它可以成为克服你本不该承受的地位劣势的绝佳工具，

sentences.en: but it's just as good if you already were born with a status privilege.
sentences.zh: 但如果你生来就享有地位特权，它同样适用。

sentences.en: So the same science and solutions are universal and they apply to everybody.
sentences.zh: 因此，同样的科学和解决方案是通用的，适用于每一个人。

sentences.en: It's just that people who have been handed disadvantage that they don't deserve could really benefit from that.
sentences.zh: 只是那些被强加了本不该承受的劣势的人，真的能从中获益匪浅。

sentences.en: So Allison, in 2021, the former Georgia State Representative Stacey Abrams was on CBS Sunday morning when she was asked the question,
sentences.zh: 所以艾莉森，在2021年，前佐治亚州众议员斯黛西·阿布朗斯做客哥伦比亚广播公司《星期日早间新闻》时，被问到了这样一个问题：

sentences.en: do you want to be president?
sentences.zh: 你想当总统吗？

sentences.en: Now, this was a very tricky question for her.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，这这是一个非常棘手的问题。

sentences.en: She had just lost her bid for governor a couple of years before.
sentences.zh: 就在几年前，她竞选州长刚刚失利。

sentences.en: So it might have been seen as overly ambitious to answer yes.
sentences.zh: 所以如果回答“想”，可能会被视为野心过大。

sentences.en: And her critics might have even said it would be delusional.
sentences.zh: 她的批评者甚至可能会说这简直是妄想。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip of her response.
sentences.zh: 我想放一段她回应的剪辑。

sentences.en: Do I hold it as an ambition?
sentences.zh: 我把它当作一种野心吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And even more importantly, when someone asks me if that's my ambition,
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，当有人问我这是否是我的野心时，

sentences.en: I have a responsibility to say yes for every young woman, every person of color,
sentences.zh: 我有一种责任去回答“是”，为了每一个年轻女性，每一个有色人种，

sentences.en: every young person of color who sees me and decides what they're capable of based on what I think I'm capable of.
